SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
Luke counts at least fifteen years of his reign (Luke 3:1).
ROMAN RECORDS
Succeeded Augustus in August AD 14; died on 16 March AD 37, 'in the seventy-eighth year of his age and the twenty-third of his reign' (Suetonius, Tiberius 73).
COUNTED FROM HIS SHARED RULE (RAMSAY 1898)
Ramsay counts from the grant of power equal to Augustus's in the provinces, at the end of AD 11, which makes the fifteenth year AD 25-26.
Counted from Augustus's death: AD 28-29
Ellicott's commentary (about 1880: "A.D. 29"); A. Plummer (1896), citing Keim and Lewin
Plummer: "No instance is known of reckoning the reign of Tiberius from his association with Augustus"; fifteen years from Augustus's death "would be A.D. 29". Luke 3:1 [17][4]
Counted from his shared rule in the provinces: AD 25-26
W. M. Ramsay (1898); A. W. Zumpt, K. Wieseler and B. Weiss (as reported by Plummer, 1896)

Tiberius received power equal to Augustus's in the provinces before the end of AD 11; counted from then, the fifteenth year is AD 25-26. Ramsay grants that this count "is never employed elsewhere in reckoning the reign of that emperor". Luke 3:1 [20][17]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 6
Luke 3 Matthew 22 Mark 12 Luke 20 Luke 23 John 19
PASSAGES · 6
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture never says Tiberius knew of Jesus or of John.
In the tribute question and at the trial Scripture says "Caesar", not Tiberius.
Scripture says nothing of his death or his successor.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON

From the textLuke 3:1 is the only verse that names Tiberius. The site's person record also gives him the 'Caesar' of the tribute question and of the trial before Pilate. Those events fall in his reign by Luke's own dating, but the verses say only 'Caesar'. Luke 3:1 Matthew 22:17–21 Mark 12:14–17 Luke 20:22–25 Luke 23:2 John 19:12 +1 more
